clue.text: Skilful answer, right?

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer
droit is a legal right, borrowed from French

explanation.surface: Someone checks that their clever reply was correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'right?' read as asking for confirmation; here it is just the noun for an entitlement, as in droit de seigneur.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit describes someone deft and clever with hands or mind, a straightforward synonym of skilful.

clue.text: Barrel containing not quite the last bit of bulgur wheat

indicators.note: the barrel word holds the selected letter inside it, so one piece sits within the other

indicators.text: not quite the last bit of
indicators.note: stopping one short of the final letter points to the second-to-last letter of the following word

blocks.note: a drum is a cylindrical barrel, as for oil
the penultimate letter of the word bulgur

explanation.surface: A cask holding nearly all of a cracked-wheat product.
explanation.walkthrough: The U goes after the D of DRUM to give DURUM; bulgur is itself made from this hard wheat, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum is a hard variety of wheat grown chiefly for making pasta and semolina.

clue.text: Attack official UK statisticians, chuckling with no sign of hesitation

indicators.note: having none of something means those letters are taken away from the word before

blocks.note: the Office for National Statistics, the UK government statistics body
chuckling is a kind of laughter
er is the noise a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: An assault on government number-crunchers who giggle without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ONS is the Office for National Statistics, the UK body that publishes official figures; er is the filler sound of a hesitant speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, sustained attack, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Suffering loss of first husband, however unlucky

indicators.note: losing the first of something means the earliest occurrence of that letter is dropped

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
though can mean however, as in 'I did it, though'

explanation.surface: A widow's bereavement is a stroke of terrible misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: THOUGH has two Hs; only the first goes, leaving TOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough is used of bad luck, as in 'tough luck' or 'that's tough', meaning unfortunate.

clue.text: Go over the limit, regularly being first to rant aboard bus

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals keeps every other letter of the next word
the first of the following word means only its opening letter is used
a passenger aboard a vehicle is inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of being
a coach is a long-distance bus
opening letter of rant

explanation.surface: A passenger on a bus starts ranting about another driver speeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over the limit' suggests speeding, but here it means trespassing; the bus is a long-distance coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude beyond proper bounds, overstepping a boundary or limit.

clue.text: Domestic appliance for keeping kippers warm

definitions.text: Domestic appliance for keeping kippers warm

blocks.clueFragment: Domestic appliance for keeping kippers warm
blocks.note: surface reading: a kitchen gadget for heating smoked herring
setter's reading: kippers are people having a kip, a British word for a nap, so sleepers

explanation.walkthrough: Kipper is a smoked herring, but to kip is British slang for to sleep, so a kipper here is someone asleep in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated pad of wiring spread on a bed keeps a sleeper cosy, so it is a household device warming nappers.

clue.text: Rail caught, breaking my new tool

indicators.note: something breaking into a line splits it apart and sits in the gap

blocks.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
N is the abbreviation for new
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a rake is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A railway line is snapped by somebody's brand-new implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a railway track or a bar, but it is a family of wading birds; cor is a British exclamation like 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake is a bird of the rail family, so rail is its classification; definition by category.

clue.text: Former university cuts, not a moment too soon

indicators.note: a piece that cuts into a word slices it open and sits inside

blocks.note: once means formerly, at some earlier time
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A one-time college finally makes spending cuts, though rather late.
explanation.walkthrough: U sits between the C and E of ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: On cue means at exactly the right moment, the idiom for something arriving just in time.

clue.text: Cancels my reordered plants

indicators.note: putting things into a new order rearranges the letters of the words before

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Someone calls off a delivery of shrubs they had ordered earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamens are flowering plants with swept-back petals, often grown as houseplants; plural matches plural.

clue.text: Urgency shown by media certain to lose face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so losing it drops the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: the press means the news media
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Journalists fear a scandal that will lose them credibility, and act with haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose face' reads as humiliation, but it simply strips the first letter of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure is the stress of demands that cannot wait, as in 'working under pressure', close to urgency.

clue.text: Fancy -- exhausted Romeo gets firm twice!

indicators.note: something exhausted has run out before the end, so the word is cut short

blocks.note: taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm, written two times

explanation.surface: A tired lover is boosted by a double helping of firmness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' runs Romeo out after two letters; the exclamation mark is just surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an elaborately ornate decorative style, so it serves as an adjective for highly ornamented, fancy.

clue.text: Busy MEP, strong but no Liberal, able to share feelings

indicators.note: a busy person is bustling around, so the letters move about too
except for one thing means that letter is removed from the word before

blocks.note: Member of the European Parliament, taken as written
athletic means muscular and strong
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A hard-working, sturdy Euro-MP from outside the Liberal party proves a sympathetic listener.
explanation.walkthrough: ATHLETIC without its L is ATHETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being empathetic means understanding and entering into how other people feel, the capacity to feel with them.

clue.text: Possibly lead away from front and elsewhere

indicators.note: taking something away from the front removes the opening letter

blocks.note: lead is one example of a metal, as 'possibly' signals

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone should take the dog's leash off the front and go somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a dog lead or taking charge, but it is the heavy element; et al. abbreviates Latin et alibi as well as et alii.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al. abbreviates the Latin et alibi, meaning 'and in other places', as well as et alii, 'and others'.

clue.text: Again, finance house primarily converts monetary unit

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the initial letters of the two words count
converting something changes it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
initial letters of finance and house

explanation.surface: A lending company changes foreign currency once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finance house' looks like a single lender, but only its two first letters join AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the currency of Afghanistan, so it is a unit of money.

clue.text: Extremely anaemic hideous canned music

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept
canned is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: first and last letters of anaemic
the word supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at feeble, ugly recorded background music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned music' looks like a phrase for piped recordings, but canned is the drunken anagram signal and music alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid house is a style of electronic dance music from the late 1980s, so music is its genre.

clue.text: Pilots and navigators perhaps packing small items for flight?

indicators.note: someone packing a thing has it stowed inside them, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: pilots and navigators are examples of members of aircrews
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Flight crews pack little things for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Items for flight' suggests luggage; the question mark flags that these items make the aircraft fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Airscrews are aircraft propellers, the parts that pull a plane through the air, hence things for flying.

clue.text: This offers digital access to other functions on board

definitions.text: This offers digital access to other functions on board

blocks.clueFragment: This offers digital access to other functions on board
blocks.note: surface reading: an onboard system, say on a ship or plane, opening online services
setter's reading: digital means done with the fingers, and the board is a keyboard

explanation.walkthrough: Digital suggests computing, but it means using a digit, a finger; 'other' hints at the alternative-function key.
explanation.definitionFit: The key labelled Alt on a computer keyboard is pressed with a finger to give other keys alternative functions.

clue.text: Northumbrian village given new frontage for shops

indicators.note: a new frontage replaces the face of a building, so the opening letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: Seahouses is a fishing village on the Northumberland coast in north-east England

explanation.surface: A seaside village gets fresh shop fronts.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the S; the definition shops pins it down as T.
explanation.definitionFit: Teahouses are establishments serving tea and light meals, a kind of shop or cafe.

clue.text: Painfully cold beer

blocks.note: first meaning: of weather, piercingly chilly
second meaning: the British hoppy draught ale

explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is the traditional British pub ale, a hoppy draught beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a biting wind or freezing day, and is also the name of a well-hopped English ale.

clue.text: Redesign bridleways after ignoring clear local rules

indicators.note: redesigning something lays it out afresh, so these letters are rearranged
ignoring part of the word means leaving those letters out before the rest is used

blocks.note: taken as written
to rid is to clear, as in rid the house of mice

explanation.surface: A council redraws the network of riding paths and cuts through its own regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove RID from BRIDLEWAYS and rearrange what remains; bridleways are British paths open to horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Byelaws are regulations made by a local council or body, applying only within its own area.

clue.text: Negative push Hugh ignored intermittently

indicators.note: dropping letters at intervals means every other one is left out of the words

blocks.note: the even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A refusal: a nudge from Hugh gets brushed off now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-uh is an informal spoken no, a grunt of refusal or denial.

clue.text: One who keeps razors uncovered

indicators.note: with its covering stripped off a word loses its outside letters, leaving the inner ones

blocks.note: razors are shavers; the plural with its outer letters gone

explanation.surface: A man stores his razors without their protective caps.
explanation.walkthrough: Razors are SHAVERS, and only the inner letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A haver is someone who has or possesses something, so a person who holds or retains it.

clue.text: Train hard by river where transport was kept?

blocks.note: to coach is to train someone
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
the Ouse is the name of several English rivers

explanation.surface: An athlete trains hard along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the railway transport hinted at later, but it is the verb to coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach house was the outbuilding where horse-drawn carriages were stored, hence transport kept there.

clue.text: Hack, for one, runs in tights

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other sits within its letters

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
hose is an old word for tights or stockings

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist jogs about wearing leggings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' wants to be a journalist; a hack is also a riding horse, which 'for one' marks as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a horse used for ordinary riding, so it is one example of the animal.

clue.text: Water carrier underneath opening of storm drain

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, being underneath means coming later in the column

blocks.note: first letter of storm
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: Rainwater runs below the grating of a storm drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water carrier' looks like the definition of a pipe, but it is the jug; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer is an underground conduit carrying waste water, so it is a drain.

clue.text: Radiation in live broadcast affected actor

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered, as seed is, so the letters are thrown about
one piece placed in the other sits within its letters

blocks.note: UV is ultraviolet radiation
the word supplies the letters

explanation.surface: An actor on air during a live show is exposed to radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live broadcast' reads as a TV term, but broadcast is the anagram signal; UV goes after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Luvvie is British slang for a gushing, self-important actor, so an affected performer.

clue.text: Our kid, at first wavering, recognised American filmmaker

indicators.note: at first means only the initial letter of the preceding word is used
wavering means unsteady, so the letters before it shift about

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of kid
to recognise is to see, so saw
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A hesitant youngster spots a US film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our kid' is northern English for a sibling, but here the words split; the answer is a Japanese director, not an American one.
explanation.definitionFit: Akira Kurosawa was the great Japanese film director of Rashomon and Seven Samurai.

clue.text: Introduction of lending rate changed fixed transfer system

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter
the word before it is altered by rearranging its letters

blocks.note: first letter of lending
the word supplies the letters
set means fixed, as in set price

explanation.surface: A bank brings in a variable lending rate and transfers its fixed one.
explanation.walkthrough: Letraset is a brand of dry-transfer lettering, rubbed onto paper, popular with designers before computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Letraset sheets carry letters that are rubbed off onto a page, a system for transferring type.

clue.text: Second cross held in palm maybe about to protrude

indicators.note: a thing held in another is gripped inside it
turning about faces the other way, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: a palm is one example of a tree
S is the abbreviation for second
X is a cross mark

explanation.surface: A cross drawn on the palm of a hand is about to stick out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm' suggests a hand but is the tree; SX goes inside TREE and the result is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Exsert is a botanical and zoological verb meaning to thrust out or project, so to stick out.
